ratings_why.fun: Choosing where news starts and who stands next to whom is a real puzzle that grows the whole board, but the halving maths makes most small Gossips look like they did nothing.
ratings_why.distinct: Gossip that fades along the Knot and Rats as glue for other tribes' bodies is fresh, but at heart it is a decaying adjacency buff close to Hedgerow's touching runs.

verdict_why: Ilse, the Knot's ends under ties and Chimney stacking can't be read as written; fixing those is a real gain, not just a change.

points.text: Ilse the Minute-Taker: say what 'biggest Gossip' means (most total stats?) and whether the repeat counts as a new Gossip that a Mill-Chimney doubles and the Seconder hears.
With ties the Knot is a graph, so 'first and last in reading order' no longer reads as its ends; say ties never change which units are the ends, so Fips and Wheel of Heads stay readable.
A +1/+1 or +2/+1 Gossip barely travels, so the tribe's main verb often looks dead; rounding up, or always reaching one step, would make every piece of news visibly spread.
The Thirty-Two of Altenburg does nothing next to We, the Rattenkönig; giving it its own job, such as keeping in-fight Gossip it hears permanently, would make both T6 cards worth reading.
Mill-Chimney Voice: say whether two Chimneys touching one source double twice, and whether the doubling happens before the halving.

standouts.why: Old Gundel reads at once and plays the fantasy: one tickle and the whole knot talks together.
Taster Wendelin tastes a neighbour's growth and passes the news on, which is the real rat behaviour turned into a clear rule.
The Winter Huddle shares each blow across the bodies tied to it, so the warm winter knot shows up in how fights go.

weakest.why: Ratskeller Landlady is a conditional 1 gold with nothing to see on the board.
The Thirty-Two of Altenburg is redundant beside the other T6 payoff.
Cold-Shed Litter is a generic summon with no Gossip in it.

flags.note: 'Biggest Gossip' and whether the repeat is doubled or heard are not defined.
Which units are the Knot's ends once ties make it a graph.
Stacking of two Chimneys, and order against halving.
Speaker Brotkrume with a Mill-Chimney and We, the Rattenkönig hands a 40/40's stats to every unit in a fight; a deliberate high roll worth the owner's eye.
Each share counting as a hit multiplies Bristle and Damage Reduction across the Knot.
